{{recipe}}

This is a recipe for a '''chicken madras'''. It is a popular curry in the [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United Kingdom|UK]].

==Ingredients==

*4 [[Cookbook:Chicken|chicken]] breasts, [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
*2 large [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]]
*4 cloves of [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Mince|minced]]
*1 jar of [[Cookbook:Tomato Paste|tomato puree]], mixed with an equal volume of water 
*2 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoons]] of ground [[Cookbook:Cayenne Pepper|cayenne pepper]]
*3 teaspoons of [[Cookbook:Garam masala|garam masala]]
*1 teaspoon of ground [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin]]
*1 teaspoon of ground [[Cookbook:Turmeric|turmeric]]
*8 [[Cookbook:Cardamom|cardamom]] pods
*½ teaspoon of ground [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]]
*½ teaspoon of ground [[Cookbook:Coriander|coriander]]
*Juice of ½ [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemon]]

=== Garnish ===

* Fresh [[Cookbook:Chiles|chiles]]
* 1 pinch of garam masala
* Freshly-chopped [[Cookbook:Cilantro|coriander leaves]]

==Procedure==
# Heat a large [[Cookbook:Frying Pan|skillet]] or [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]] over medium heat, and add a liberal amount of cooking oil. When at temperature add the chopped onions. Cook the onions for a couple of minutes until they start to brown slightly.
# Add the minced garlic, cayenne pepper, and garam masala. Stir for 2 to 3 minutes.
# Add the ground cumin, ground turmeric, ground ginger, and ground coriander. Stir in for about 30 seconds.
# Add the diced chicken. Cook, stirring, until the chicken is cooked through.
# Add the diluted tomato puree and the seeds from the 8 cardamom pods. Stir, then lower the heat and place a lid on the saucepan.
# [[Cookbook:Simmering|Simmer]] for 30 minutes stirring occasionally. If the sauce starts to stick to the pan add some water.
# Remove the lid and squeeze the juice of half a lemon into the pan along with a pinch of salt. Stir and let simmer uncovered for 10 to 15 minutes.
# Serve with garnishes.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* Other meats can be substituted for the chicken.
* This dish currently has a heat level of a hot masala. To bring the heat up to about a madras level, add approx ½ teaspoon of [[Cookbook:Chili Powder|chili powder]] when adding the cayenne pepper.
